Title: AKU alumni coauthors atlas of congenital heart diseases
NewsSummary: The Color Atlas and Synopsis of Adult Congenital Heart Disease
NewsContent:
Alumus Dr Ali N Zaidi MBBS '99 has coauthored The Color Atlas and Synopsis of Adult Congenital Heart Disease, a resource for paediatricians, internists, family practitioners and medical students. 

Why an Atlas? Dr Zaidi said that he drew on his experiences at AKU where, as a medical student, he had the opportunity to care for a number of 'blue babies', children born with  congenital defects.

"In the developed world, more than 95 percent of children born with congenital heart disease now survive. That was not the case perhaps even 30 years ago. The survival rates are such that with appropriate therapies - they not only survive the newborn period, but reach adulthood - which is where I come in," says Dr Zaidi who is an Adult Congenital Heart Disease specialist.

But children with congenital heart defects born in the developing world where appropriate cardiac therapies may not be available, die within the first year or the first few years of their life. This is why the work with congenital heart disease is so important.

"I always wanted to write a 'simple' book for a very 'complex' topic," says Dr Zaidi. With a "case based" approach and high quality images the atlas will help improve the diagnostic process and result in early diagnosis and improved treatment in a country like Pakistan - with 56,000 such cases every year - where there are only 30 paediatric cardiologists and seven paediatric cardiac surgeons.

Dr Zaidi completed his combined Internal Medicine and Paediatrics residency at The Penn State Hershey Medical Center, and then did combined fellowships in Paediatric Cardiology and Adult Cardiovascular Disease at the Nationwide Children's Hospital and The Ohio State University Medical Center. During these five years he also completed specialized training in Adult Congenital Heart Disease (ACHD) and Pulmonary Hypertension. Dr Zaidi is currently the Director of the Montefiore Adult Congenital Heart Disease and Pulmonary Hypertension Program at the Montefiore Einstein Center for Heart & Vascular Care and The Children's Hospital at Montefiore, at the Albert Einstein College of Medicine in New York.
